identity.title: Fever-induced OR560 promotes antibacterial immunity through macrophage pseudopod formation and phagocytosis.

content.abstract: Fever is a conserved physiological response to pathogen infection. However, how fever promotes host defense remains poorly understood. Here we find that fever empowers antibacterial immunity by inducing olfactory receptor 560 (OR560) to promote macrophage phagocytosis. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we discovered that OR560 is indispensable for macrophage phagocytosis. Febrile temperature drives the serum response factor-dependent OR560 induction in macrophages to boost phagocytosis. OR560 responds to bacteria-derived peptides and plays an essential role in mediating pseudopod formation-a key step required for target uptake. Modulation of body temperature in mice showed that the immune-amplifying effect of fever depends predominantly on OR560. We further demonstrated that the genetic ablation of either Olfr560 or serum response factor (Srf) in mice not only abolished fever-potentiated macrophage phagocytosis but also led to catastrophic defects in bacterial clearance and increased mortality upon infections. Thus, our work reveals that OR560 is a pivotal regulator of fever-enhanced antibacterial phagocytosis and integrates both pathogen-derived and febrile signals to ensure a robust response to infection.
